springs.helical_spring_rate.title: Helical spring rate and index
assumptions: Round wire, linear elastic, mean coil diameter D constant. n_a is the number of active coils (total minus the inactive end coils). C ≳ 4 is the usual design range.

springs.spring_stress.title: Helical spring shear stress with Wahl and Bergsträsser correction

variables.name: tau_w
variables.desc: corrected shear stress using Wahl factor
variables.label: τw

variables.name: tau_b
variables.desc: corrected shear stress using Bergsträsser factor
variables.label: τb

assumptions: Correction factors combine the direct (transverse) shear and the wire-curvature effect. Naming varies between texts — (4C−1)/(4C−4) + 0.615/C is the Wahl factor and (4C+2)/(4C−3) the (simpler) Bergsträsser factor; both are given.
8FD/(πd³) is the uncorrected shear stress; both corrected stresses are reported.
method_references: Wahl and Bergsträsser stress-correction factors; τ = K·8FD/(πd³) (recalled)

springs.spring_deflection.title: Helical spring deflection under axial load
assumptions: Linear elastic; δ = F/k with k from helical_spring_rate. Physical helical geometry needs the spring index C = D/d ≥ 1 (D ≥ d); C is reported so a non-physical D < d is rejected rather than silently computed.

springs.spring_geometry.title: Helical spring total coils, solid and free length

procedure.python:
def _spring_geometry(values):
    """Total coils, solid length and free length from active coils and the end condition."""
    d = values['d']
    na = values['n_a']
    end = values['end']
    if end not in _END_OFFSET:
        raise MechError(f'end: {end!r} is not one of {", ".join(sorted(_END_OFFSET))}')
    add, solid_extra = _END_OFFSET[end]
    nt = na + add
    ls = d * (nt + solid_extra)
    return {'n_t': nt, 'L_s': ls, 'L_f': ls + values['delta_max']}

assumptions: End condition sets the total-coil count and solid length: plain n_t = n_a (L_s = d(n_t+1)); plain-and-ground n_t = n_a+1 (L_s = d·n_t); squared (closed) n_t = n_a+2 (L_s = d(n_t+1)); squared-and-ground n_t = n_a+2 (L_s = d·n_t).
L_f = L_s + δ_max is the minimum free length (solid length plus working travel); it is not the pitch-based manufactured free length (which follows from the coil pitch and end configuration).
method_references: Solid/free length by end condition (Shigley Table 10-1, recalled)

springs.spring_buckling.title: Compression spring buckling (critical deflection and stability)

variables.name: delta_cr
variables.desc: critical deflection at buckling onset (null when stable)
variables.label: δcr

variables.name: alpha
variables.desc: end-condition constant (0.5 fixed-fixed, 0.707 hinged, 1.0 free, 2.0 fixed-free)
variables.label: α

procedure.python:
def _spring_buckling(values):
    """Compression-spring buckling: critical deflection, absolute-stability length, stable flag.

    Shigley form δ_cr = C₁′·L0·[1 − √(1 − C₂′/λ_eff²)] with C₁′ = E/(2(E − G)),
    C₂′ = 2π²(E − G)/(2G + E) and λ_eff = α·L0/D. Buckling is possible only when
    L0 ≥ L0_crit = (πD/α)·√(2(E − G)/(2G + E)); for L0 < L0_crit the spring is absolutely
    stable and δ_cr has no real value (reported null, stable = 1).
    """
    L0, D = values['L0'], values['D']
    E, G = values['E'], values['G']
    alpha = values['alpha']
    if alpha <= 0:
        raise MechError('spring_buckling: alpha (end-condition constant) must be positive')
    if E <= G:
        raise MechError("spring_buckling: Young's modulus E must exceed the shear modulus G")
    c1 = E / (2.0 * (E - G))
    c2 = 2.0 * PI ** 2 * (E - G) / (2.0 * G + E)
    L0_crit = (PI * D / alpha) * math.sqrt(2.0 * (E - G) / (2.0 * G + E))
    if L0 < L0_crit:
        return {'L0_crit': L0_crit, 'delta_cr': None, 'stable': 1}
    lam = alpha * L0 / D
    delta_cr = c1 * L0 * (1.0 - math.sqrt(1.0 - c2 / lam ** 2))
    return {'L0_crit': L0_crit, 'delta_cr': delta_cr, 'stable': 0}

assumptions: Spring treated as a column with an equivalent flexural rigidity. δ_cr = C₁′·L0·[1 − √(1 − C₂′/λ_eff²)] with C₁′ = E/(2(E−G)), C₂′ = 2π²(E−G)/(2G+E), λ_eff = α·L0/D. Buckling is possible only for L0 ≥ L0_crit = (πD/α)·√(2(E−G)/(2G+E)); a shorter spring is absolutely stable (stable = 1, δ_cr null). At exactly L0 = L0_crit the critical deflection is C₁′·L0_crit.
Compression springs only; squared-and-ground ends ≈ fixed (α = 0.5).
method_references: Spring buckling / stability criterion (Shigley sec. 10-4 form, recalled)

springs.spring_surge.title: Helical spring surge (natural) frequency
assumptions: Fundamental surge mode of the spring alone (its own mass). f is for both ends fixed, f = ½√(k/m_s) with m_s = ρ·π²d²D·n_a/4 (active-coil mass) and k = Gd⁴/(8D³n_a); one end fixed and the other free gives f_free = ¼√(k/m_s) = f/2. With an attached mass m, use f ≈ (1/2π)·√(k/(m + m_s/3)).

springs.extension_hook_stress.title: Extension spring hook stresses (sections A and B)

variables.name: sigma_A
variables.desc: maximum stress at hook section A (bending + direct tension)
variables.label: σA

variables.name: tau_B
variables.desc: maximum shear stress at hook section B (torsion)
variables.label: τB

variables.name: r1
variables.desc: inner radius of the hook loop at section A

variables.name: r2
variables.desc: inner radius of the hook loop at section B

assumptions: Section A is where the hook joins the coil body: bending moment F·D/2 (plus the direct tension F) with the curvature factor K_A = (4C₁²−C₁−1)/(4C₁(C₁−1)), C₁ = 2r₁/d. Section B is the hook end loaded in torsion (torque F·D/2) with K_B = (4C₂−1)/(4C₂−4), C₂ = 2r₂/d. Requires C₁, C₂ > 1 (hook bend radius larger than the wire radius).
method_references: Extension-spring hook bending and torsion; curvature factors (Shigley sec. 10-9 forms, recalled)

springs.torsion_spring.title: Helical torsion spring rate, deflection and stress

variables.name: k_t
variables.desc: ideal torsional spring rate per radian

variables.name: k_turn
variables.desc: ideal torsional spring rate per turn (2π·k_t)

variables.name: k_prime
variables.desc: empirical rate per turn with friction allowance (Shigley)

variables.name: sigma
variables.desc: maximum bending stress at the inner surface
variables.label: σ

variables.name: M
variables.desc: applied moment (torque) at the spring ends

assumptions: Wire in bending (coils wind/unwind). k_t = Ed⁴/(64·D·N_a) N·m/rad is the ideal straight-wire rate per radian (θ = M·L_w/(EI), L_w = π·D·N_a); the ideal per-turn rate is k_turn = 2π·k_t = Ed⁴/(10.19·D·N_a) N·m/turn. Shigley's empirical rate k_prime = Ed⁴/(10.8·D·N_a) N·m/turn adds a friction allowance. Active coils include the end legs: N_a = N_b + (l₁ + l₂)/(3πD). K_i = (4C² − C − 1)/(4C(C−1)) corrects the inner (compressive) surface; the outer surface is tensile for a spring wound to tighten.
method_references: Torsion spring rate θ = M·L_w/(EI) (straight-wire bending); per-turn rates; end-leg coil correction; inner-fibre stress factor (Shigley sec. 10-6 forms, recalled)

springs.leaf_spring.title: Multi-leaf (semi-elliptic) leaf spring deflection and stress
assumptions: Graduated (equal-stress) leaf idealisation with N leaves sliding without friction and equal thickness t. The 3/8 deflection factor is the uniform-strength result (1.5× the constant-section beam value); σ is the leaf-surface stress.

springs.belleville.title: Belleville (disc) spring load and deflection

variables.name: form
variables.desc: geometry constant: K1 (DIN 2092) or M (original Almen–László)

variables.name: K
variables.desc: geometry constant (K1 for DIN 2092, M for original Almen–László)

assumptions: Almen–László load–deflection for a coned disc: F = 4E·δ/((1−ν²)·K·D_o²)·[(h−δ)(h−δ/2)·t + t³]. The geometry constant K is either K1 (DIN 2092) = (1/π)((C−1)/C)²/((C+1)/(C−1) − 2/ln C) or the original Almen–László M = (6/(π·ln C))·((C−1)/C)² — the same theory with two conventions for the neutral circle; they differ by under 1 % for typical C. Valid for 0 ≤ δ ≤ h (flat at δ = h; flattening then snap-through beyond the flat position is not modelled). The load–deflection curve is non-monotonic (snap-through) when h/t ≳ √2.
method_references: Almen–László disc-spring equation: F = 4Eδ/((1−ν²)K·D_o²)·[(h−δ)(h−δ/2)t + t³], DIN 2092 K1 and original Almen–László M (recalled)

springs.spring_energy.title: Elastic energy stored in a spring
assumptions: Linear spring: U = F·δ/2 = k·δ²/2 = F²/(2k).
method_references: U = Fδ/2 (area under the linear force–deflection curve)

springs.spring_fatigue.title: Spring-wire fatigue safety factors (Goodman and Gerber)

variables.name: S_ut
variables.desc: ultimate tensile strength of the wire (S_ut = A/d^m)

variables.name: S_se
variables.desc: fully reversed torsional endurance, Goodman conversion of Zimmerli-type data

variables.name: S_se_gerber
variables.desc: fully reversed torsional endurance, Gerber conversion S_sa/(1 − (S_sm/S_su)²)

variables.name: A
variables.desc: wire strength coefficient (S_ut at d = 1 mm; Shigley Table 10-4 A/d^m)

variables.name: S_sa
variables.desc: torsional endurance amplitude from Zimmerli-type data

variables.name: S_sm
variables.desc: mean stress of the Zimmerli-type data

procedure.python:
def _spring_fatigue(values):
    """Spring-wire fatigue: wire strength, torsional endurance and Goodman/Gerber safety factors.

    S_ut = A/d^m with d in mm and A in MPa·mm^m (wire-strength table, Shigley Table 10-4 form); in
    coherent SI this is S_ut = A·(1 mm/d)^m with A = S_ut at d = 1 mm (Pa). S_su = 0.67·S_ut.
    Zimmerli-type test data (S_sa, S_sm measured at a nonzero mean stress) convert to the fully
    reversed endurance with the SAME criterion that is then applied: Goodman S_se = S_sa/(1 − S_sm/S_su) and
    Gerber S_se,G = S_sa/(1 − (S_sm/S_su)²). Goodman and Gerber safety factors then follow for the working
    alternating/mean shear (τ_a, τ_m).
    """
    d, A, m = values['d'], values['A'], values['m']
    S_sa, S_sm = values['S_sa'], values['S_sm']
    tau_a, tau_m = values['tau_a'], values['tau_m']
    if d <= 0:
        raise MechError('spring_fatigue: wire diameter d must be positive')
    if A <= 0:
        raise MechError('spring_fatigue: strength coefficient A must be positive')
    S_ut = A * (1e-3 / d) ** m
    S_su = 0.67 * S_ut
    if S_sm >= S_su:
        raise MechError('spring_fatigue: S_sm must be less than S_su (0.67·S_ut) '
                        'for the Zimmerli conversion')
    if S_sa <= 0:
        raise MechError('spring_fatigue: S_sa must be positive')
    S_se = S_sa / (1.0 - S_sm / S_su)               # Goodman conversion
    S_se_gerber = S_sa / (1.0 - (S_sm / S_su) ** 2)  # Gerber conversion (consistent with the Gerber criterion)
    if tau_a < 0 or tau_m < 0:
        raise MechError('spring_fatigue: tau_a and tau_m must be >= 0')
    if tau_a == 0 and tau_m == 0:
        raise MechError('spring_fatigue: tau_a and tau_m cannot both be zero')
    n_goodman = 1.0 / (tau_a / S_se + tau_m / S_su)
    a = (tau_m / S_su) ** 2
    b = tau_a / S_se_gerber
    if a > 0:
        n_gerber = (math.sqrt(b * b + 4.0 * a) - b) / (2.0 * a)
    else:
        n_gerber = 1.0 / b if b > 0 else float('inf')
    return {'S_ut': S_ut, 'S_su': S_su, 'S_se': S_se, 'S_se_gerber': S_se_gerber,
            'n_goodman': n_goodman, 'n_gerber': n_gerber}

assumptions: Wire strength S_ut = A/d^m with d in mm and A in MPa·mm^m (Shigley Table 10-4 form); enter A as the strength at d = 1 mm (Pa) and m the table exponent. S_su = 0.67·S_ut. Zimmerli-type test data (S_sa, S_sm — e.g. unpeened ≈ 241/379 MPa, peened ≈ 398/534 MPa — are user inputs, not built in) convert to the fully reversed endurance S_se = S_sa/(1 − S_sm/S_su). Compute τ_a, τ_m from the load range with spring_stress (τ = K·8FD/(πd³) at F_max and F_min). Goodman: 1/n = τ_a/S_se + τ_m/S_su; Gerber: n·τ_a/S_se,G + (n·τ_m/S_su)² = 1 with the Gerber-converted S_se,G (solve the quadratic).
method_references: Wire strength S_ut = A/d^m (Shigley Table 10-4 form, recalled); S_su = 0.67·S_ut; Zimmerli-type fully-reversed conversion S_se = S_sa/(1 − S_sm/S_su); Goodman and Gerber in torsion (recalled)

source.derivation: Squared-and-ground: n_t = n_a + 2 = 12; L_s = d·n_t = 0.004·12 = 0.048 m; L_f = L_s + δ_max = 48 + 60 = 108 mm
Plain-and-ground: n_t = n_a + 1 = 9; L_s = d·n_t = 0.005·9 = 0.045 m; L_f = L_s + δ_max = 45 + 40 = 85 mm
L0_crit = (πD/α)·√(2(E−G)/(2G+E)) = (π·0.032/0.5)·√(255.4/365.6) = 0.168049 m. L0 = 0.100 m < L0_crit, so the spring is absolutely stable: stable = 1 and δ_cr has no real value (null)
Reversing the moment sign flips θ and σ (signed) but leaves the rate: θ = M/k_t = −2/5.27736 = −0.378978 rad; σ = K_i·32M/(πd³) = −353.406 MPa; k_t unchanged at 5.27736 N·m/rad
Inverse: solve the Almen–László load for δ at the known load F = 46165.9 N (the DIN 2092 branch). The forward point δ = 3 mm reproduces this load, so the recovered deflection is 3 mm

Same S_se = 336.073 MPa. With τ_m = 0 the criteria reduce to n = S_se/τ_a: Goodman 336.073/100 = 3.36073; Gerber uses its own conversion S_se,G = 261.965 MPa → n = 2.61965 (the two differ only through the Zimmerli conversion)
